A1.justification: Both 19-page PDFs describe the same QuestA work and include Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QuestA training and benchmark results in Section 4, a dataset ablation in Section 5, and additional empirical analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for QuestA-trained models in Tables 2–4 and training analyses in Figures 4–8, including Appendix C. These results are retained from v1.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A.1 retain identical partial-solution augmentation, the fixed 50% hint ratio, GRPO/DAPO integration, training objective and reward function.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenR1-Math-220K and OpenMathReasoning for training and retain the same mathematics, coding, general-knowledge and logic evaluations in Sections 4–5 and Tables 2–4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical throughout Tables 1–4. Table 2 retains DeepScaleR, Nemotron, DeepSeek-R1-Distill at 1.5B/7B/32B, and Qwen3 at 1.7B/8B.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical data selection, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures, including the 32,768-token generation limit, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95 and evaluation without hints.

E4.justification: The dataset ablation in Section 5, cross-domain tests in Table 3, and training-dynamics and problem-success analyses in Figures 4–8 are unchanged, including the analyses in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the same unbiased pass@k estimator and n >= 2k sampling rule. Reporting of sampling counts is unchanged; neither version reports training-seed repetitions, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–4 and all plotted results match. For example, Table 2 retains QuestA-Nemotron-1.5B scores of 67.08%, 59.50% and 35.52% on AIME24, AIME25 and HMMT FEB 25, respectively.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions and learnability results in Section 3 and the proofs in Appendix B are identical. No mathematical condition, theorem or derivation is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about expanded reasoning capacity, improved pass@1/pass@k, state-of-the-art 1.5B mathematics performance and improved sample efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving sample efficiency and entropy remain identical. The qualification that the theory guarantees training success and the data-curation limitation discussed in Figure 8's caption are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain identical preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and prompt templates. Code and dataset access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 and all 43 references are unchanged, including the positioning of partial-solution augmentation as orthogonal to changes in RL algorithms and reward design.

P1.justification: On page 1, v2 removes Ant Research from the affiliations of Jiazheng Li, Jiaxuan Gao and Yi Wu, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body prose, terminology, section order and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: Shortened affiliations slightly alter horizontal spacing and alignment within the page 1 author block. Figures 1–8, Tables 1–4, their captions and all page layouts from page 2 onward are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision only changes affiliation information, author-block spacing and the arXiv stamp. The scientific narrative, methods, evidence, theory and reproducibility details, including Appendices A–C, remain identical. These administrative edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
